units.title: Carrow Point: the rain's going
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:10 readings. Pressure 1004 hPa and rising fast, 5 hPa in six hours. Wind veering south-west 3. Rain 6 mm overnight, light now, and a clear edge visible on the western horizon. Three-day total at the station: 79.6 mm, the wettest three days since I put the gauge in. Expect it dry by mid-afternoon and a cold, very clear night. Frost by the weekend.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: I've now searched the registry for every name and every reference on the list. None of the references exist in any format the registry uses. Two of the properties have owners who are not Ardent Vale or any company connected to it. One purchase predates the company's incorporation. I can't find a single filing that matches. This is my last post in this thread. I'd suggest that nobody shares the list any further.

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, something nice. My late husband's roses on the balcony have one bud left, in November, which they have never done before. It is a small pink one, rather tight, and I do not know if it will open. I have moved it out of the wind and I say good morning to it. Thank you, Bev, for this thread. Irena, 7C

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Thank you all, and to the fitter for the miners' rule. A clear night here at last, the first in a week, and very cold. I kept the door shut and watched the stars from inside, through glass that I'd cleaned so well that for a moment I forgot it was there. The beam went out its full length tonight. Nothing in it but the cliff path and a sheep.

units.title: Tonight's top three calls (anonymised, obviously)
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Top three calls of the night. Three: a man who wanted to know whether he could pay his bill 'in instalments of one'. Two: a lady whose meter was 'making a face at her' (it was showing the error code that looks like a frown). One: a caller who just wanted to tell somebody that his power had stayed on all week and he was grateful. I logged that one as 'feedback, positive'. First time this month.

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref KE/DC/0473. Further to notice KE/DC/0471, a contractor will inspect and adjust self-closing devices on stair landing fire doors on floors 5 to 9 next Thursday between 09:00 and 15:00. Access to the stairwell will not be restricted. This work is in preparation for the scheduled fire risk inspection. We thank residents for their patience and cooperation.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: So the 7th is accounted for, and I'm glad, and I'm grateful to the young man for saying so. It explains one night. It doesn't explain the 4th, which was high water with the slip nearly covered, and it doesn't explain Lisle on the 10th. My view hasn't changed: those were most likely people too. We now know who one of them was. We don't know who the others were.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Rethinking, which is what real researchers do. If the radar station really was sold to the bird people, then Ardent Vale is selling off its other refuges and putting everything into the Holm. That's why the clearance is so rushed. The others were never good enough. The Holm is the one they're keeping. Updated version going out to my list today.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Bearing, for what it's worth. From the starboard rail of the 17:50, coming round toward Gilliver at half six, you'd be looking roughly north-east, across the Lisle channel at the Lisle boatyard. They had sawn timber delivered on Monday for the slip repairs, stacked under the yard light by the gate. I'd start there before the Holm, or the fish market.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Yesterday this was a network of five refuges, all bought at once. This morning it's one refuge and four sales. Both can't be true, and the list supports neither, because the list doesn't check out. What would we expect to see if Ardent Vale were selling property? Sale filings. Planning Watcher looked. There aren't any.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Thank you, Mr Ferrous. I said before that my old pupils on the ferry are not people who make things up, and nothing this week has changed my mind. I'd also say the young man's apology was well written. Clear, short, no excuses. I've marked worse from university graduates.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: An update from Lisle. The Women's Institute met last night and agreed to put together parcels for the crew, if an address can be found: socks, fruit cake, a flask, some newspapers. Mrs Penrose has already started a scarf in a colour she describes as 'safety orange'. We are knitting regardless, on the principle that wool is never wasted.

units.title: Notice: slipway report (update)
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Following a public statement by a local young person, I can confirm that one report of a person on the Gilliver slipway, on the night of the 7th, has been accounted for. I have spoken with the young person and his family, and he has apologised. The matter is closed, and I'd ask that he be left alone. Byelaw 14(2) remains in force. Thank you.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: For those asking who he is: it's the Rowe lad from the chippy, the sixth-former at Port Ammet College, his family's on the harbour road. Not saying it to shame him. Saying it because people deserve to know who's been feeding them a story and whether anyone put him up to it.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I have removed a post which named the young person, his family and his school. He is seventeen, he has apologised in public under his own handle, and the harbourmaster has closed the matter. Naming him adds nothing but harm. Further posts of that kind will be removed and the account suspended.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: For the record, from our side: Odell's crew weren't on the 7th. That was the relief crew's report, the one logged as 'person on slip, no response, fog'. So the lad explains that log entry, and good on him. It doesn't touch the 4th, which was us, and it doesn't touch Lisle.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Afternoon all. Just popping in on my lunch to say: kid in a coat. Thank you, thank you. Signed copies of my original post available from the showroom, Tollinby ring road, ask for Cal. Free air freshener with every apology.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: The bird people own the radar station. That's it. Case closed. Ledger, mate, your correspondent at the 'law firm' is having you on, and Gil is having himself on. I've been right twice in two days and I'm starting to scare myself.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Gracious? I've been called a troll on this board for a month for saying it was a kid. I'll be gracious when the ferry company says sorry for the welfare review. Nice apology though, I'll give the lad that. Better than any I've had.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Good for him for owning it. But I want this written down here, where people who matter read it. He's not who I hailed on the 4th. The 4th was high water, he wasn't there, and he says so himself. What I hailed was taller than me, and I'm five ten. He's five eight in his socks; he's served me chips every Friday for two years. I'm not angry with him. I'm angry with everyone using him to say I made it up.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: I accept Planning Watcher's points about the references, and I'm sorry that I posted before I could answer them. I've written to my correspondent and had no reply. I am rechecking Lyme Dale and Skellan Rock, which look the weakest of the six entries. I still think Tarrow Fort and Hask Quarry are worth looking at, and I'll post properly when I have something firmer.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: For accuracy: Ardent Vale has issued a statement today about what it calls 'recent inaccurate reports of our wider portfolio'. The Courier has published it in full; the link is attached. Please quote it accurately if you discuss it. Please don't paraphrase it into something it doesn't say, in either direction.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: The rain stopped about three and the island looked very close afterwards in the clean air, the way it does before a frost. I can see more of the hill than I used to. I hope the young people out there had a dry afternoon. My lamp is on already. Mrs Hale, if the parcels go, I would like to put in some of my shortbread.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: The mitten has gone home. A little girl called Effie knocked on my blue door with her mother after school and said 'that's my snowflake one' through the letterbox. Her granny made it, as I thought. She has promised to keep both of them on a string from now on. Thank you to the board for letting me post about such a small thing.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: well that's one of them explained. grudgingly. the lad came in the chandlery this morning with his dad and apologised to me as well, which he didn't have to do, I only sell rope. that's the end of it on here lads. anybody who wants to argue about the other nights can take it to the Sound Board

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: seth: orange oilskins on order, due next boat. red-light head torches in now, two set aside behind the counter with your name on in marker. tell the new lad to stop leaning on the stern rail in a swell, it's not the oilskins' fault

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Read the company statement in the courier on my tea break. Then read it again. Then my missus read it. Still don't know if they own a fort or not. In my trade if you can't say whether you own a digger, you don't own a digger, simple as.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Ferrous may well be right. I asked at the Lisle boatyard on my way home. They did have sawn timber delivered on Monday, and it is under the yard light by the gate, though the man said 'not that much, mind'. My wife says she is still right. I have stopped arguing with either of them and gone back to complaining about the 07:40.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Kerris on the boat this morning was quieter than I've ever seen her. I'd ask everyone going round saying 'it was all a kid' to read what the kid actually wrote: one night, the 7th, not the 4th, not Lisle. He was more careful about it than half the people quoting him.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Rain's gone. Out at first light and the Sound flat as a plate after it, everything brown from the burns. Prices up a touch, restaurants are ringing again. Lost no creels this time. Saw timber in the water off the Holm side, three or four lengths, drifting with the ebb. Reported it to Quill.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lad's grandad would have skelped him for borrowing that coat. Good on him for saying it, though. Doesn't change what Kerris saw on the 4th, mind. She's been on that boat longer than he's been alive, and she's never once told me the sea was calmer than it was.

units.title: Logs in the channel
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you to those who reported floating timber this afternoon between Gilliver and the Holm. The Coastguard has issued a notice. From reports, there are at least four lengths of roundwood, three to five metres long, drifting with the tide. Please give them a wide berth, especially after dark, and report positions to the harbour office rather than trying to tow them in.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: and before anybody says it, lads, logs come down every burn on this coast after three days of rain like that, the Brackwater burn alone took half a fence and a footbridge rail. no need for a theory. a four metre log will still put a hole in a creel boat, mind, so watch it

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see? Storm wood from the burns is usually broken, with root plates or snapped ends and bark hanging off. Felled timber has clean saw cuts at both ends. If anyone gets close enough in daylight to see the ends, that would tell us where it came from. Without that, I wouldn't guess.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: First clear evening in a week. Visibility now more than 30 km, and from the point you can see the Holm in real detail: the ridge, the camp lights coming on, the bare ground on the slopes. Temperature dropping fast, 5 C at 20:00 and heading for frost. Wrap up, whoever's out there.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: I shan't telephone again. On reflection, a man has a right to his quiet, and I would not like to be the old fellow who rang twice. I shall simply leave a cup of tea out in spirit, as it were, and wait. Regards, Ned

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: Kerris I know. I'm not the one from the 4th and I never said I was, I wasn't even in Gilliver, I was at my dad's. I only did it once. I'm sorry people are using what I said to make out none of it happened. That's not what I meant at all. Also yes it's every Friday, large chips, no vinegar.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Short note: dunlin is fine. He messaged me this evening. He's taking a break and he'll post when he's ready. Please be kind to him when he does, and please don't ask him for more than he offers. Thank you to the keeper, to tern, to Ned and to everyone who stayed sensible in this thread.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: oh thank god. ok. ok. sorry for all the posts, everyone, I know I filled the thread up. I'm going to make a cup of tea and sit down and not refresh this for at least ten minutes. probably five.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones off, shoulders down. Thank you, quaver. Tern, five minutes is fine. I've been refreshing it from the hospital break room all week, so you're in good company. Glad he's fine. Glad you all are.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good. Ordinary outcome, as these usually are. For what it's worth, the way this thread behaved is the way I'd want one to behave about me: practical questions, a keeper with a gate log, and a mod who kept the guessing out. Well done, all.

units.title: Back (sorry)
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Hi all. I'm fine. I'm sorry for the worry, and thank you to the keeper, to tern and to Ned especially. What happened is embarrassing. During the session I dropped my phone in the reservoir off the outflow boards, which is why my channel went dead. I didn't go back for the car that night. I stayed with my brother in Tollinby, and he drove me over at five the next morning to fetch it. Make of it what you will.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Kit status, since people will ask. The handheld survived in its case. The two omnis are fine. The phone did not survive, and with it went my session notes for the last night, gain settings and all. LB-2611 can stay marked incomplete. I'd rather it did. I'll be off the forum for a bit after this.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I'm really glad. really. but I walked to position two in the rain looking for you, with the keeper, at seven in the morning. your brother has a phone? I'm not angry. I'm a bit angry. mostly glad. sorry. I'll be normal tomorrow.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: You're right, and I'm sorry. My brother has a phone and I should have used it to tell you, at least. I wasn't thinking straight that night, and by the next day I was too embarrassed to post. That's not a good reason. Thank you for going out there. I owe you more than a pint.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Welcome back. Phones and reservoirs have a long history together. One question, and feel free to ignore it: your last note said 'moving to two, back in ten', and you never got back to the session. Why did you leave the position early? Purely out of interest in the recording.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Welcome back. For the record, a phone floats for about four seconds before it goes, face down, every time. Ask me how I know. Two of mine are in Gilliver harbour and one's in a creel off the Holm side. Glad it was only the phone.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: I'd rather not talk about why I left early. I left, I dropped the phone on the boards on the way out, and that's the order it happened in. I know that's not a satisfying answer for a recording thread. It's the one I've got, and I'd be grateful if we left it there.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok. not asking. not asking ever. glad you're back, young man (that's from Ned, who will be asleep, but he'd say it). see you at the reservoir in daylight sometime. I'll bring two phones.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Thread stays open, but please respect what dunlin has said about leaving early. Questions about the recordings themselves are fine. Questions about why he left are not, unless he raises it himself. Welcome back, and take as long a break as you need.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys this is insane, the recordist who vanished at the reservoir is back and won't say why he left?? I need the raw file from position two, I'm doing a full breakdown video this weekend, link in bio, drop it in my messages bro, you'll get full credit I promise

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Removed a request for dunlin's files for a video. NightScreamLive, you have already been temp-banned once for re-uploading other people's recordings. Please don't make it twice. Files in the catalogue are there for listening and study, not for channels.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be reading it wrong. But the statement says early on that they 'do not hold, and have never held' the properties named, and then further down that 'those sites are managed separately'. I don't see how you manage something separately that you've never held. Sorry, I'm not trying to start anything. I just read it three times.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Finally someone sees it... 'Never held' and 'managed separately' in the same breath. That's not a denial. That's a company that's been told what to say and can't keep it straight. I told you the list was real. The details were wrong because they were meant to be.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: The sky cleared tonight, and you can see the camp lights much more sharply now, like they're closer. All the lamps along the front were lit too. I counted 31 lit windows from mine, which is more than I've ever counted. I don't know what that means. Probably only that it's cold and dark at five.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I've put a box of paperbacks by the shop door with a note in Mrs Hale's direction, in case the parcels go. Fourteen books. I took out the one with the shipwreck in it, on reflection, and put in a cookery book instead. Nights out there must be long enough without shipwrecks.
